Title: Fold Layer-specific Learning Rates: Optimizing Training Dynamics in PPO with Soft Fold Layers

Name: input_dependent_hyperplane_combination
Title: Input-Dependent Hyperplane Combination in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Adaptability in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to learn a set of basis normal vectors and combine them based on input-dependent weights. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a learnable matrix 'N' of shape (num_basis, width), where num_basis is a hyperparameter. Add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a softmax activation) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a weight vector of shape (num_basis,). The forward pass will compute the weighted sum of the basis normal vectors using these weights: n = sum(weights[i] * N[i]) for i in range(num_basis). Normalize the resulting vector 'n' to ensure it has unit length. The forward pass will then use this dynamically combined 'n' to compute the folding effect. Experiment with different values for num_basis (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and different architectures for the weight prediction network (e.g., adding a hidden layer, using different activation functions). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed 'n'.

Name: weighted_prototype_softfold
Title: Weighted Prototype-Modulated SoftFold Layers: Adaptive Combination of Directional Prototypes in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to incorporate multiple learnable prototype vectors. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a learnable matrix 'P' of shape (num_prototypes, width), where num_prototypes is a hyperparameter. In the forward pass, compute the cosine similarity between the input tensor and each prototype vector in 'P'. Use these similarities to modulate the crease and stretch parameters of each prototype's folding operation. Specifically, scale the original crease and stretch parameters by the similarity score for each prototype. Perform the soft folding operation for each prototype using these adjusted parameters, resulting in 'num_prototypes' output vectors. Introduce a learnable weight for each prototype's output. Implement these weights as a linear layer with 'num_prototypes' inputs followed by a softmax activation. Multiply each prototype output vector by its corresponding weight, and sum the resulting weighted output vectors. Experiment with different values for num_prototypes (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and different similarity measures (e.g., RBF kernel). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a single normal vector.

Name: input_dependent_crease
Title: Input-Dependent Crease Modulation in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Adaptability in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to dynamically adjust the crease parameter based on the input tensor. The second linear layer will take the hidden representation as input and output a scaling factor for the existing crease parameter. The final layer will use a Tanh activation function. The forward pass will compute the output of this network and multiply it with the original crease parameter. The adjusted crease parameter will then be used in the subsequent calculations within the SoftFold layer. Experiment with different hidden layer sizes. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed crease.

Name: weighted_ensemble_softfold
Title: Weighted Ensemble of SoftFold Layers: Enhancing Representation Capacity with Learnable Weights in PPO
Experiment: Modify the Agent class to incorporate a weighted ensemble of SoftFold layers. Replace the existing SoftFold layers in both the actor and critic networks with 'num_folds' SoftFold layers, where 'num_folds' is a hyperparameter. Each SoftFold layer will have its own independently learned normal vector 'n', crease, and stretch parameters. Introduce a learnable weight vector of shape (num_folds,). These weights will be implemented as nn.Parameter and initialized randomly. In the forward pass of the Agent, compute the output of each SoftFold layer in the ensemble. Then, multiply each SoftFold layer's output by its corresponding weight from the learnable weight vector. Sum the resulting weighted outputs to obtain the final output of the ensemble. Experiment with different values for 'num_folds' (e.g., 2, 4, 8). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a single SoftFold layer.

Name: input_modulated_softfold
Title: Input-Modulated SoftFold Layer: Adaptive Folding with Input-Dependent Crease and Stretch in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to dynamically adjust the crease and stretch parameters based on the input tensor. Introduce a modulation network that takes the input tensor as input and outputs scaling factors for the crease and stretch parameters. This modulation network will consist of two linear layers (linear-ReLU-linear-Tanh) for each parameter (crease and stretch), resulting in four linear layers in total. The first linear layer for each parameter will take the input tensor as input and output a hidden representation. This will be followed by a ReLU activation function. The second linear layer will take the hidden representation as input and output a scaling factor for the corresponding parameter (crease or stretch). The final layer will use a Tanh activation function. The forward pass will compute the outputs of these networks and multiply them with the original crease and stretch parameters, respectively. The adjusted crease and stretch parameters will then be used in the subsequent calculations within the SoftFold layer. Experiment with different hidden layer sizes. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using fixed crease and stretch.

Name: concatenated_state_and_input_dependent_crease
Title: Concatenated State and Input-Dependent Crease Modulation in Soft Fold Layers
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to dynamically adjust the crease parameter based on both the input tensor and the agent's state. Introduce two separate modulation networks: one for the input tensor and one for the agent's state (represented by the hidden activations of the preceding layers). The agent state modulation network will consist of a linear layer to reduce the dimensionality of the hidden activations, followed by a Tanh activation function. The input modulation network will consist of a linear layer followed by a Tanh activation function. Concatenate the outputs of the two modulation networks. Feed the concatenated output into a single linear layer that outputs the final scaling factor for the crease parameter. The forward pass will compute the outputs of these networks, concatenate them, and then pass the result through the final linear layer to obtain the scaling factor. This scaling factor will then be multiplied with the original crease parameter. The adjusted crease parameter will then be used in the subsequent calculations within the SoftFold layer. Name: gated_softfold_transformed_input

Name: vonmisesfisher_modulated_crease
Title: SoftFold Layers with von Mises-Fisher Modulated Crease: Adaptive Folding Strength in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to use the mean direction of a von Mises-Fisher (vMF) distribution as the normal vector 'n' and modulate the crease parameter with the concentration parameter 'kappa'. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with two learnable parameters: a mean direction vector 'mu' (of the same dimension as the input) and a concentration parameter 'kappa' (a scalar). The 'mu' vector will represent the mean direction of the vMF distribution, and 'kappa' will control the concentration around the mean direction. Normalize 'mu' to have unit length. In the forward pass, use 'mu' directly as the normal vector 'n' in the SoftFold operation. Multiply the original crease parameter by a function of 'kappa' (e.g., sigmoid(kappa), tanh(kappa), or simply kappa itself). The adjusted crease parameter will then be used in the subsequent calculations within the SoftFold layer. Experiment with different initial values for 'kappa' (e.g., 0, 1, 10) and different functions to modulate the crease parameter. Also experiment with making kappa input-dependent by introducing a small neural network that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a scaling factor for kappa. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed 'n' and fixed crease.
